guide.summary: Customer-by-customer OAuth fits the read-only use case: each customer authorizes separately and selects the pages the integration can read. Because customers in other organizations/workspaces will connect, the integration must be public rather than limited to selected workspaces. The read content capability is required for reading page content. Provider review and marketplace distribution requirements are not established by the supplied snapshots.

findings.title: Each customer authorizes through the OAuth flow and receives a user-tied access token
findings.detail: OAuth integrations are for apps that act on behalf of each person who uses them. Each user authorizes the app separately, and the app uses an access token tied to that user for all subsequent API requests. Authorization is per user, so each customer in each workspace must complete the flow individually.
findings.appliesWhen: Customers connect their own Notion accounts to the web app.

steps.title: Confirm the consent prompt and redirect callback for one customer
steps.detail: Send a test customer to the authorization URL from the Configuration tab. The prompt shows the connection capabilities; the customer selects the pages to share through the page picker and clicks Allow access. Notion redirects to the redirect URI with a code parameter. Confirm the callback receives code and that a denied request returns an error parameter instead. Do not treat this step as consent granted by the assistant.
steps.doneWhen: The redirect URI receives a code query parameter after a selected-page approval, and a cancelled attempt returns an error parameter.

steps.title: Exchange the authorization code for an access token
steps.detail: Post the temporary code to the token endpoint using HTTP Basic authentication with CLIENT_ID:CLIENT_SECRET base64 encoded. The JSON body includes grant_type set to authorization_code, the code from the redirect, and the redirect_uri. The response contains access_token, refresh_token, bot_id, owner and workspace fields; store all of them. Expected success output is a JSON object with access_token.
steps.doneWhen: The token endpoint returns HTTP 200 with access_token, refresh_token and workspace_id, and the tokens are stored server-side.

steps.title: Read one customer-shared page as markdown
steps.detail: Using the access token from the representative customer and the ID of a page that customer shared in the page picker, request the page markdown. The response has a top-level markdown string with the page content and a truncated boolean. When truncated is true, some blocks were omitted and unknown_block_ids lists the affected block IDs, so record that flag rather than treating the content as complete. A missing capability returns 403 and an unshared page returns 404.
steps.doneWhen: HTTP 200 returns a markdown string for a shared page and the truncated value is recorded. Boundary check: inspect the actual grant against the documented access above; confirm the outgoing request log contains only GET requests to the markdown endpoint and no prohibited actions.

Permissions : The page contains child pages or other content that is not shared with the connection.

fields: page_id: a page the customer shared in the page picker
ACCESS_TOKEN: access_token from the OAuth token response for that customer

steps.title: Read the title of one customer-shared page
steps.detail: Using the same shared page ID and the same customer's access token, request the page object with filter_properties=title so the properties object is limited to the title property. Pages that are not in a data source return only title. In the properties object, find the property whose type is title and read its text content. The exact nested field path is not documented in the supplied text, so confirm it from a real response rather than assuming a path. Do not read other properties or content blocks in this step.
steps.doneWhen: HTTP 200 returns a page object and the title text is read from the property whose type is title. Boundary check: inspect the actual grant against the documented access above; confirm the outgoing request log contains only GET requests to the page endpoint and no prohibited actions.

evidence.quote: string[] Property names or IDs to include in each page's properties object. Other properties are left out. Repeat the parameter to pass more than one value, for example filter_properties=title&filter_properties=Status .
Pages that aren't in a data source always return only title .
For a page in a data source, the property values follow that data source’s schema . For a page whose parent is another page, the only property is title .

steps.doneWhen: A page the customer did not share returns HTTP 404 and no page content.

details.title: Each customer authorizes through the OAuth flow and receives a user-tied access token
details.detail: OAuth integrations are for apps that act on behalf of each person who uses them. Each user authorizes the app separately, and the app uses an access token tied to that user for all subsequent API requests. Authorization is per user, so each customer in each workspace must complete the flow individually.
details.appliesWhen: Customers connect their own Notion accounts to the web app.

preparation.title: Permissions rationale
preparation.text: read content: Candidate only. The markdown read step is supported by documented read content scope and $.markdown/$.truncated fields, but read-page-title-representative claims a title value from the properties object, which is not in its documentedResponseFields and whose nested path the guide says is undocumented, so the source needs a documented title text path (e.g., properties[title-type property].title[].plain_text) before the title read can be approved.

preparation.title: Registration worksheet
preparation.text:
Create a public OAuth integration in the Notion Developer portal
Open the Developer portal, select Connections under Build, and create a new connection with Any workspace installation scope so customers in other workspaces can install it. Installation scope cannot be changed later. Enter the redirect URI for the web app.
Fields: Installation scope: any workspace (public), Redirect URI: your web app callback URL

Draft: Enable only the read content capability on the integration
Draft setup only — confirm the access mapping before selecting permissions or authorizing an account. In the Configuration tab, scroll to the Capabilities section and enable read content. Leave write and administration capabilities disabled because the use case is read-only and prohibits page modification and workspace administration.
Fields: Capability: read content only

preparation.title: First connection test
preparation.text:
Confirm the consent prompt and redirect callback for one customer
Done when: The redirect URI receives a code query parameter after a selected-page approval, and a cancelled attempt returns an error parameter.

Exchange the authorization code for an access token
Done when: The token endpoint returns HTTP 200 with access_token, refresh_token and workspace_id, and the tokens are stored server-side.

Read one customer-shared page as markdown
Done when: HTTP 200 returns a markdown string for a shared page and the truncated value is recorded. Boundary check: inspect the actual grant against the documented access above; confirm the outgoing request log contains only GET requests to the markdown endpoint and no prohibited actions.

Read the title of one customer-shared page
Done when: HTTP 200 returns a page object and the title text is read from the property whose type is title. Boundary check: inspect the actual grant against the documented access above; confirm the outgoing request log contains only GET requests to the page endpoint and no prohibited actions.

Confirm an unshared page is not readable
Done when: A page the customer did not share returns HTTP 404 and no page content.
